hero.lead: SPT connects a wearable sensor (GPS 20 Hz outdoors, UWB indoors), smartwatch, chest strap and smart scale to a platform that calculates load, readiness and injury risk in real time — for a whole squad or a single amateur athlete.

show.title: Coastline United SC: one match week with SPT
show.sub: An illustrative scenario of a professional club in California: how a staff of around thirty people works from Monday to match day with a single source of truth.

days.x: The morning wellness questionnaire (sleep, fatigue, muscle soreness, mood) and HRV from the watch arrive before breakfast. Every player gets a readiness score of 0–100; those in the red get an individual recovery plan.

The vest measures distance by speed zone, sprints, accelerations and PlayerLoad. The strength & conditioning coach sees live who is below and who is above the target dose for that day of the microcycle.
The AI model combines ACWR, readiness, stride asymmetry and injury history. Player #6 shows an ACWR of 1.52 and a 38 % load spike — the staff reduces his minutes before an injury happens.
The edge server at the stadium receives 22 sensors in real time. The bench sees speeds, heart rate, sprints and alerts; the analyst in the control room compares two players on a half-pitch view.
Automatic match and weekly reports: top 5 by load, new flags, recovery recommendations. Print or PDF for the coach, a mobile summary for the player.

hw.title: Hardware that measures what matters
hw.sub: Every device carries the SPT mark and sends data into the same athlete record — no manual copying.

items.x: A body-fitted compression vest; the sensor stays still against the back, so the GPS trace and accelerations are clean. Washable, breathable, sizes from youth categories upwards.
items.w: A poorly fixed sensor means noise in acceleration data and false sprints.

items.x: The sensor sits between the shoulder blades — the steadiest point of the body while running, with the best view of the sky for satellite signal.
items.w: Sensor placement directly determines the accuracy of speed and load.

items.x: GNSS 20 Hz (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou), 9-axis IMU up to 1000 Hz, UWB and BLE in an IP67 housing. It switches from GPS to UWB automatically when play moves indoors.
items.w: Impacts, landings and changes of direction last milliseconds — 1000 Hz captures them.

items.x: Heart rate, HRV, sleep and daily recovery; a vibration alerts the athlete when they leave the target zone. For amateurs, the watch alone is the whole SPT.
items.w: HRV is the most sensitive non-invasive indicator of fatigue and recovery.

items.x: Beat-by-beat heart rate for interval training, water polo and rowing — where an optical wrist sensor gets it wrong.
items.w: TRIMP and heart-rate zones require an exact R-R interval.

items.x: Bioimpedance: weight, muscle, fat, water, visceral fat and basal metabolic rate — straight into the athlete record and the meal planner.
items.w: Losing 2 % of body mass to dehydration measurably reduces performance.

items.x: Anchors on the arena ceiling deliver position with roughly ±10 cm accuracy where GPS cannot work: volleyball, basketball, handball, futsal, hockey.
items.w: UWB measures the time of flight of radio pulses in nanoseconds and is robust against signal reflections.

items.x: A stadium server receives every sensor, calculates metrics locally and sends them to the bench in under a second — even when the internet fails.
items.w: A substitution decision must not wait for the cloud.

sci.title: Key features — what they do and why they matter
sci.sub: Behind every number in SPT is a method from sports science. These are the most important ones.

items.what: For every athlete SPT calculates the ratio of acute (7-day) to chronic (28-day) load from GPS metrics and perceived exertion (sRPE × minutes).
items.why: Sudden load spikes are associated with a higher risk of soft-tissue injuries. A zone of roughly 0.8–1.3 is considered the 'sweet spot', while values above ~1.5 call for caution (Gabbett, British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2016). SPT colours every player green, amber or red — before training, not after an injury.

items.what: The model combines ACWR, daily readiness, wellness, stride asymmetry, injury history and age into a single risk score from 0 to 100 and lists the main contributing factors.
items.why: An injury is rarely caused by one number. Combining signals gives an early warning with an explanation — the staff decides, the model assists. SPT is a decision-support tool, not a medical diagnosis.

items.t: Hybrid positioning: GPS outdoors, UWB indoors
items.what: Outdoors the sensor uses multiple satellite systems at 20 Hz; indoors UWB anchors measure the time of flight of radio pulses and deliver positions with roughly ±10 cm accuracy. AUTO mode picks the source by itself.
items.why: Indoor sports make up half of the sporting world, and GPS does not work under a roof. The same metric outdoors and indoors means comparable data across the whole season.

items.what: The IMU measures the ground contact time of the left and right foot (GCT) and countermovement jump (CMJ) height over time.
items.why: Rising left–right asymmetry and a drop in CMJ often precede overload. SPT raises a flag when asymmetry exceeds 6 % — time for the physiotherapist, not another sprint.

items.what: Every injury gets a protocol: pain control → range of motion → strength → running → sport-specific work → full training. Each step has a criterion and a physiotherapist's sign-off.
items.why: Returning too early is a common cause of re-injury. Criteria instead of the calendar — and the whole staff sees the same status.

items.what: Sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, muscle soreness, stress and mood combine into one number with a traffic light.
items.why: The same session for a tired and a rested player is not the same session. Readiness sets the dose of the day.

items.what: Female athletes log their cycle phase and SPT gives phase-specific recommendations: volume, intensity, recovery and nutrition.
items.why: Hormonal changes affect thermoregulation, recovery and perceived exertion. Individualisation instead of averages.

sci.disclaimer: SPT is a performance-tracking and decision-support system; it does not replace a medical examination or diagnosis.

items.q: Is SPT only for professional clubs?
items.a: No. The same system works for a professional club, an academy and an amateur athlete. An amateur needs only the watch and the app; a club adds vests, UWB anchors and an edge server.
Yes. Indoors it uses UWB anchors with roughly ±10 cm accuracy, outdoors GPS at 20 Hz. AUTO mode switches the position source by itself.

items.q: Is the AI injury prediction a medical diagnosis?
items.a: No. It is an early-warning and decision-support system that shows risk factors. The decision is always made by the professional staff.
The club and the athlete. Clubs are stored under codes, access is defined by roles, and data can be exported at any time (CSV, JSON, API).

items.q: Can manufacturers use SPT under their own brand?
items.a: Yes. SPT is licensed as white-label: your brand, our tools, software and servers. SPT already runs inside other manufacturers' devices.
On Windows with one click (a desktop shortcut), on phones and tablets as a PWA from the browser, and on the web with no installation.
The app is available in 10 languages, and this page in 24.
